text: The other lads' account of Monday evening and the night
why: ¶20 places the two other lads at the trainer's house for supper on Monday evening, so their account of that evening is a plain question the story gives reason to consider.
¶20 says Edith Baxter carried Hunter's supper to the stables and carried a lantern, so asking for her account is a reasonable question.
¶20 says Ned Hunter remained on guard at the stables that night, so his account is a reasonable question.
¶20 names the maid as Edith Baxter.
¶20 names the lad on guard as Ned Hunter.
¶19–20 state there were three lads, two of whom walked to the trainer's house while the third, Ned Hunter, stayed on guard.
¶20 says the path to the stables ran across the open moor.
¶20 says Hunter's supper consisted of a dish of curried mutton.
¶20 says the maid carried down Hunter's supper, which was the curried mutton.
¶20 says the maid carried a lantern with her.
¶20 says there was a water-tap in the stables, and the lad on duty was to drink nothing else.

text: The kitchen of the trainer's house
why: ¶20 says the two lads had supper in the kitchen of the trainer's house.
¶20 and the opening refer to last Monday night and 'that evening'.
¶20 says the stables were locked up at nine o'clock on Monday.
¶20 says the maid carried the supper down at a few minutes after nine.
